passages.text: NERVOUS FEVER, or SLOW FEVER, a fever of the continued kind, which comes on slowly, with chilliness, heaviness, headach, and a great dejection of spirits.
The pulse is quick and weak, the tongue dry; and as the disease goes on, the patient falls into great weakness, with a low muttering delirium and a trembling of the hands.
It is described by Dr Huxham under the name of the slow nervous fever, and it may last three or four weeks.
Most physicians consider it the same disease as the putrid or jail fever, differing from it only in degree, as being milder in its beginning and slower in its course.
Some who have opened the bodies of those dead of this fever have found the inner coat of the bowels inflamed and ulcerated; but whether this be the cause or the effect of the fever is not yet known.
The causes are thought to be grief, anxiety, low spirits, fatigue, and the breathing of close and corrupted air, as in crowded and damp houses.
The cure depends chiefly on supporting the strength by wine, Peruvian bark, and a nourishing diet; bleeding is seldom proper.
Typhoid fever is a disease caused by the bacterium Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi. Symptoms usually begin 6 to 30 days after exposure, often with a gradual onset of high fever over several days.
The fever is often accompanied by weakness, abdominal pain, constipation and headache. In severe cases people may become confused.
Without treatment, the illness classically passes through stages that each last about a week.
The bacteria spread by eating or drinking food or water contaminated with the faeces of an infected person. Poor sanitation and poor hygiene are risk factors.
The bacteria invade the lining of the small intestine, including the lymphoid tissue called Peyer's patches. Ulcers there can bleed or perforate the bowel.

Typhoid and typhus were long thought to be one disease. The name typhoid means resembling typhus. In 1837 William Wood Gerhard of Philadelphia showed that they are different, and William Jenner confirmed it in England around 1850.
Antibiotics such as azithromycin, fluoroquinolones and third-generation cephalosporins are used to treat it. Resistance to antibiotics is a growing problem.
Vaccines against typhoid are available. Clean drinking water, sanitation and hand washing prevent its spread.

reasons: The old headword names a type of fever by its symptoms, not a single disease, so the match is loose.
The slow onset, the length of three or four weeks and the ulcers of the bowels point to typhoid fever.
Typhus also scores, because the 1823 entry treats both as one disease.

alignments.label: The name nervous fever

britannica.quote: under the name of the slow nervous fever

wikipedia.quote: The name typhoid means resembling typhus

alignments.note: A change in language. The old name describes the symptoms. Inference: in 1823 nervous fever probably covered typhoid and some milder cases of typhus.

alignments.label: Same as typhus

britannica.quote: the same disease as the putrid or jail fever, differing from it only in degree

wikipedia.quote: In 1837 William Wood Gerhard of Philadelphia showed that they are different

alignments.note: A change in knowledge. Typhoid and typhus are different diseases with different bacteria. Physicians separated them after 1823.

alignments.label: Ulcers of the bowels

britannica.quote: the inner coat of the bowels inflamed and ulcerated

wikipedia.quote: Ulcers there can bleed or perforate the bowel

alignments.note: The finding of some 1823 anatomists holds. Wikipedia places the ulcers in the small intestine.

alignments.label: Grief and bad air

britannica.quote: grief, anxiety, low spirits, fatigue, and the breathing of close and corrupted air

wikipedia.quote: food or water contaminated with the faeces of an infected person

alignments.note: A change in knowledge. A bacterium in food and water causes the disease, not grief or bad air.

alignments.label: Wine and bark

britannica.quote: supporting the strength by wine, Peruvian bark, and a nourishing diet

alignments.note: A change in knowledge. Antibiotics replaced wine and bark, which do not act on the infection.

alignments.label: Vaccine and clean water

wikipedia.quote: Clean drinking water, sanitation and hand washing prevent its spread

alignments.note: The 1823 entry has no prevention. Wikipedia adds vaccines and sanitation.
